body.p: Claims 1-9 and 12-24 are pending in this application. By this Amendment, claims 1, 12, 13, 15, and 20 are amended, and claims 10 and 11 are cancelled. Support for the amendments can be found in, for example, paragraphs [0015] and [0050] and Figures 1, 2, 4A, and 4B of the application as originally filed. No new matter is added. Reconsideration and allowance in due course is respectfully requested.
The Examiner is thanked for the indication that claims 23 and 24 would be allowable if rewriften in independent form.
Claim 13 is objected to due to an informality. It is respectfully submitted that the
amendment to claim 13 is responsive to the Examiner's comments, and thus the objection should be withdrawn.

Claims 1-9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 103(a) as allegedly anticipated by Sato et al. (U.S. 2022/0274693, hereinafter "Sato") in view of Rock (U.S. 2006/0102777, hereinafter "Rock). It appears, based on the remarks following this statement of rejection in the Office Action, that it was the Examiner's intention to also reject claims 11-13, 19, 21, and 22 under 35 U.S.C. @ 103(a) over Sato in view of Rock. Claim 11 has been cancelled. This rejection, insofar as it applies to claims 1-9, 12, 13, 19, 21, and 22, is respectfully traversed.

As discussed during the interview and acknowledged in the Office Action, Sato and Rock, alone or in combination, do not disclose or suggest all of the features recited in independent claim 1, or the claimed combination of features. For example, as conceded by the Office, Sato and Rock, alone or in combination, do not disclose or suggest an aircraft, including "a plurality of vertical lift propulsor assemblies, each of the plurality of vertical lift propulsor assemblies comprising a propulsor coupled to the aircraft and driven by an electric motor including a rotor and a stator, the propulsor including a hub coupled to a shaft of the rotor and a plurality of blades each extending outward from the hub, the hub being coupled to a shaft that is driven by the rotor, the hub and the plurality of blades being formed as a single element such that a blade angle of the plurality of blades of the propulsor is not individually adjustable," as recited in independent claim 1, nor "a cyclic control assembly, comprising an actuator; and a push rod extending through the shaft coupling the rotor to the propulsor, wherein the push rod is coupled to the actuator and the propulsor; the push rod is configured to increase the blade angle of the plurality of blades of the propulsor in response to a displacement of the push rod in a first direction; and the push rod is configured to decrease the blade angle of the plurality of blades of the propulsor in response to a displacement of the push rod in a second direction," as recited in independent claim 1.
The Office Action combines Sato and Rock with Deloyer (U.S. 2021/0147091,

hereinafter "Deloyer") in rejecting now-cancelled claim 10, alleging that Deloyer discloses the claimed "propulsor including a hub and a plurality of blades each extending outward from the hub...the hub and the plurality of blades being formed as a single element." However, as discussed during the interview, it would not have been obvious to modify the system disclosed by Sato, alone or in combination with Rock, to incorporate a propulsor "including a hub and a plurality of blades each extending outward from the hub, the hub and the plurality of blades being formed as a single element such that a blade angle of the plurality of blades of the propulsor is not individually adjustable," as recited in independent claim 1. Rather, as discussed during the interview, incorporation of a propulsor defined by a such a monolithic structure would render the individual blade pitch control systems disclosed by Sato and/or by Rock inoperable, destroying the utility and functionality of those systems as originally intended. It is
respectfully submitted that Sato and Rock teach away from such a modification.

For at least these reasons, it is respectfully submitted that independent claim 1 allowable over the applied combination, and thus the rejection of independent claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) over Sato and Rock should be withdrawn. Dependent claims 2-9, 12, 13, 19, 21, and 22 are allowable at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which they depend, as well as for their additional features.

Claims 14-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly unpatentable over Sato and Rock in view of Howes (U.S. 2022/0153407, hereinafter "Howes"). Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly unpatentable over Sato and Rock in view of Deloyer. Claim 10 has been cancelled. These rejections, insofar as they apply to claims 14-18, are respectfully traversed.

Dependent claims 14-18 are allowable over Sato and Rock, alone or in combination with Deloyer, at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which they depend, as well as for their additional features, and Howes fails to overcome the deficiencies of Sato, Rock, and Deloyer. For at least these reasons, it is respectfully submitted that claims 14-18 are allowable over the applied combination, and thus this rejection should be withdrawn.

It is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance and notification to that effect is earnestly requested. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned to facilitate prosecution of this application.

It is believed that all of the rejections have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Finally, nothing in this document should be construed as intended to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this document, and the amendment of any claim does not necessarily signify concession of unpatentability of the claim prior to its amendment.
If necessary, please charge any additional fees or credit overpayment to Deposit Account No. 50-3521, referencing Attorney Docket No. 0253-098001.
